extracted.intended_audience: general readers of Walt Whitman; poets, critics, theatre and music enthusiasts, and literary readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative observations on composing poetry (esp. Leaves of Grass / Good-Bye my Fancy) and on theatrical and musical performance, including principles for criticism and what makes acting, singing, and stagecraft effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: H. Heine's two principles of criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: H. Heine's first principle of criticising a book was, What motive is the author trying to carry out, or express or accomplish? and the second, Has he achiev'd it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a two-question test when judging a work: (1) identify the author's intended motive or purpose; (2) evaluate whether the work successfully realizes that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory of Leaves of Grass composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory of my Leaves of Grass as a composition of verses has been from first to last ... to thoroughly possess the mind, memory, cognizance of the author himself, with everything beforehand--a full armory of concrete actualities, observations, humanity, past poems, ballads, facts, technique, war and peace, politics, North and South, East and West, nothing too large or too small, the sciences as far as possible--and above all America and the present--after and out of which the subject of the poem ... has been invariably turned over to his Emotionality, even Personality, to be shaped thence; and emerges strictly therefrom, with all its merits and demerits on its head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose by equipping the author-mind with broad concrete material (facts, techniques, sciences, geography, history) and then let Emotionality/Personality shape the subject; accept that style will often 'smack of the living physical identity' and may be offensive to conventions. The criterion for success includes fidelity to this method and the resulting organic emergence of the poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of Good-Bye my Fancy
rubrics_metrics.description: This new last cluster, Good-By my Fancy ... the clef is here changed to its lowest, and the little book is a lot of tremolos about old age, death, and faith. The physical just lingers, but almost vanishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and judge this work by its low register, thematic focus on old age/death/faith, its garrulous and irascible tone (compared to old Lear), and its use of breaks and 'tricks' to avoid monotony; it 'will have to be ciphered and ciphered out long.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Study a play/libretto before seeing it
rubrics_metrics.description: I always studied a play or libretto quite carefully over, (sometimes twice through) before seeing it on the stage; ... I found I gain'd most by getting that sort of mastery first, if the piece had depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For deep works, pre-reading the text yields better mastery and appreciation than only seeing the stage performance; trying both approaches showed the pre-read method as superior for pieces with depth. Anti-pattern: relying solely on surface/first impressions from a performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting: realism, pathos, and artistry beyond mere technique
rubrics_metrics.description: His renderings were first-rate in everything. He inaugurated the true 'Rip Van Winkle,' and look'd and acted and dialogued it to perfection ... there was in that original performance certainly something of a far higher order, more art, more reality, more resemblance, a bit of fine pathos, a lofty brogue, beyond anything afterward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate actors on their ability to produce artful, realistic performances with genuine pathos and character-specific details (voice, brogue, resemblance), not merely technical polish. Beware of performances 'adjusted to please popular audiences' that lose higher artistic qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective stage spectacle combines grand appointments with realistic acting
rubrics_metrics.description: It was an immense show-piece, too; lots of grand set scenes and fine armor-suits and all kinds of appointments imported from London (where it had been first render'd.) The large brass bands--the three or four hundred 'supes'--the interviews between the French and English armies-- ... The death-scene of the King ... Kean rush'd in, gray-pale and yellow, and threw himself on a lounge ... His pangs were horribly realistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spectacle (elaborate sets, costumes, large bands, many supernumeraries) can create powerful effect, but the climactic emotional impact depends on realistically embodied acting. Both production scale and believable performance are criteria for an effective theatrical experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singing/music: brilliant style and deep expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Jenny Lind ... She had the most brilliant, captivating, popular musical style and expression of any one known; ... there is something in song that goes deeper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge singers by both technical brilliance and the depth of expression that penetrates listeners; excellence in singing is not merely ornament but communicative power. Use celebrated performers (Jenny Lind) as exemplars of the ideal combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry in its highest aspect serves essential Religion
rubrics_metrics.description: In its highest aspect, and striking its grandest average, essential Poetry expresses and goes along with essential Religion--has been and is more the adjunct, and more serviceable to that true religion ... than all the priests and creeds and churches that now exist or have ever existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider poetry's highest value in how it communicates and supports fundamental spiritual or religious sensibilities; evaluate poetry for depth of moral/spiritual insight rather than mere ornament or 'love-sigh' prettiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to represent the American 'bulk' or average in literature
rubrics_metrics.description: If I were ask'd persona to specify the one point of America's people on which I mainly rely, I should say the final average or bulk quality of the whole. ... my main and chief however indefinite claim for any page of mine w'd be its derivation, or seeking to derive itself, f'm that average quality of the American bulk, the people, and getting back to it again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate or produce works that fairly reflect or represent the collective character and experience ('bulk') of American people; success includes capturing those common, average qualities rather than only elite or singular perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary aim: avoid mere amusement; seek substantive contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: How difficult it is to add anything more to literature--and how unsatisfactory for any earnest spirit to serve merely the amusement of the multitude!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess literary work by whether it adds something substantive or original to literature rather than merely entertaining; prioritize depth, significance, and advancement of human understanding over ephemeral amusement.
